feat_image_vector — MULTIVAR features op

• Data kinds: images → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.feat_image_vector(images=None, features=('mean', 'std', 'p01', 'p99', 'rms_contrast', 'michelson_contrast', 'grad_energy', 'laplacian_var'), data_range=None, unit='DN', roi=None) -> 'dict' (implementation को सीधे call करना हो तो import multivar; multivar.feat_image_vector(images=None, features=('mean', 'std', 'p01', 'p99', 'rms_contrast', 'michelson_contrast', 'grad_energy', 'laplacian_var'), data_range=None, unit='DN', roi=None) -> 'dict', registry से लेना हो तो opsmultivar.get("feat_image_vector"))

उपयोग

images -> feature table {"matrix" (N, F), "names", "units", ...}, हर image की एक पंक्ति।

> नीचे का विस्तृत विवरण मूल text में है — सारांश और headings का अनुवाद हो चुका है।

The bridge from pictures to the multivariate ops: each image becomes a row of named numbers with units, ready for mv_pca / mv_pls / rsm_fit. Features (see FEATURES): mean, std, p01, p50, p99, rms_contrast, michelson_contrast, grad_energy, laplacian_var need no range; saturated_fraction, dark_fraction, entropy_bits need data_range=(lo, hi) — the range of the *sensor or format* (e.g. (0, 4095) for 12-bit), which the data cannot tell: the brightest pixel of a dim image is not the white level. It is therefore required, never inferred, and pixels outside it are refused (the range given is then wrong).

unit names the grey-level unit ("DN" by default) used in the unit strings. roi=(r0, r1, c0, c1) restricts every feature to that window (same for all images).
